# aether_cluster_network (Resource)

The network policy of an `aether_cluster`: which source addresses may reach its public control-plane endpoint, and the API-server connection rate limit. There is exactly one policy per cluster. Creating this resource OVERWRITES whatever policy the cluster has (for example one set in the portal) with the configuration; import to adopt an existing policy instead. Destroying this resource OPENS the cluster's public endpoint to any source address and resets the API-server rate limit to the platform default. The platform applies the policy asynchronously; this resource never waits for enforcement. Do not set `create_before_destroy` on this resource: a replacement of the same cluster would run the destroy, which opens the endpoint, after the create.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "cluster_id" {
  type = string
}

# Creating this OVERWRITES the cluster's current policy; destroying it OPENS the
# public endpoint to any source address. Entries must be canonical IPv4 prefixes.
resource "aether_cluster_network" "this" {
  cluster_id = var.cluster_id
  authorized_cidrs = [
    "203.0.113.0/24",
    "198.51.100.7/32",
  ]

  api_server_rate_limit = {
    max_connections_per_second = 50
    burst                      = 100
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `authorized_cidrs` (List of String) Source-address allowlist in CIDR notation (e.g. `203.0.113.0/24`, `198.51.100.7/32`). An empty list (`[]`) accepts connections from ANY source address; authentication still applies. Each entry must be an IPv4 network address in canonical form (no host bits set and no leading zeros, so `10.0.0.0/8`, not `10.0.0.1/8` or `10.0.0.0/08`) and appear only once: the API accepts the other spellings, IPv6 and duplicates, but the platform's cluster schema accepts only IPv4 network prefixes without duplicates, so the platform would keep enforcing the previous policy; those are refused at plan time (or at apply, for an entry not known until then).
- `cluster_id` (String) UUID of the `aether_cluster` the policy belongs to. Changing it replaces the resource, which first OPENS the old cluster's endpoint (see the resource description).

### Optional

- `api_server_rate_limit` (Attributes) API-server connection rate limit. Omit it for the platform default; removing it resets the limit to that default. The rate limit takes effect only when the cluster's control-plane proxy is (re)created; a running proxy keeps the limit it booted with. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_server_rate_limit))
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `cluster_id` (the policy has no id of its own).
- `updated_at` (String) Time the policy was last written (RFC 3339). A never-configured cluster reads `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`.

<a id="nestedatt--api_server_rate_limit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_server_rate_limit`

Required:

- `burst` (Number) Connections allowed in a burst above the per-second rate (1-2147483647).
- `max_connections_per_second` (Number) New connections per second allowed (1-2147483647).


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
